root_idea.summary: The root denotes good fortune, welfare, and joy, in contrast with ill fortune and misery.
root_idea.development: Its central idea develops from personal felicity and favorable circumstances to auspicious days and stars, divine enabling, mutual assistance, and several names based on benefit, favorable form, or resemblance.

senses.definition: To be made prosperous, fortunate, happy, or felicitous.
senses.usage_conditions: Quranic passive Form I usage; in 11:108 it describes those granted felicity, in contrast with the wretched, with felicity understood as divine enabling to attain good.

senses.definition: Prosperous, fortunate, happy; a person who enjoys or attains felicity.
senses.usage_conditions: Used substantively in the Quranic contrast with شَقِيّ (wretched); the fullest felicity is associated with Paradise, while the term can concern religious and worldly welfare.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To be or become prosperous, fortunate, happy, or felicitous.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Intransitive Form I usage, contrasted with شَقِيَ, with respect to religion or worldly affairs.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become auspicious, fortunate, or favorable.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of a day, star, or asterism, in opposition to becoming unlucky or inauspicious.

other_classical_meanings.definition: For water to come naturally upon the land and flow over its surface.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Describes water arriving unsought, without a machine raising it for irrigation.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To aid, assist, or help another.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Form III assistance in any manner or circumstance; the expression can suggest two people joining their efforts. One reported extension applies it to diligently carrying out God's command and good pleasure.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To assist another in lamentation and weeping for the dead.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized use in mourning; it is the assistance referred to in the report that prohibits such إسعاد.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To render someone prosperous, fortunate, happy, or felicitous; to increase his good fortune.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Causative Form IV, commonly with God as the subject.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To aid, assist, accommodate, or dispose someone toward the right course.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An alternative causative use attributed to a classical authority.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To seek after the plant called سَعْدَان.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Form V plant-related usage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To deem or reckon someone or something fortunate, auspicious, or lucky.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: May be constructed with بِهِ or with a circumstance such as seeing someone.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become fortunate by means of someone or something.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A Form X use expressing the source or means through which good fortune is obtained.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To seek good fortune through someone or something.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A Form X use focused on pursuing auspiciousness rather than merely judging something fortunate.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To desire or demand another's aid or assistance.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A separate Form X construction with a person as the requested source of help.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Prosperity, good fortune, auspiciousness, or favorable outcome.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used as an abstract noun or simple substantive, equivalent to يُمْنٌ; it can also serve as the verbal noun of the Form I verbs.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Prosperous, fortunate, or auspicious.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An epithet applied especially to a day, star, or asterism, with inflectional use differing according to the construction.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A name for Venus and Mercury and for a group of ten named asterisms, several of them lunar mansions.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The named stars include سعد الذابح, سعد بلع, سعد السعود, and سعد الأخبية, among others; the naming is associated with auspiciousness.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The name of an object of idolatrous worship associated with the sons of Milkān.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A proper name referring to a pre-Islamic cult object.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The virginity or hymen of a girl or woman.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A metonymic expression.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A fortunate or liked thing, or an unfortunate or disliked thing.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A proverbial expression used when asking whether an event is good or bad, and by extension in concern for a relative.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Aiding you repeatedly; repeated readiness to serve or support your cause.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Fixed in لَبَّيْكَ وَسَعْدَيْكَ and related formulas, with the dual form expressing repetition.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The third part or gore of the body of a shirt.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A garment term; its diminutive denotes a fourth part.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A sweet-smelling root or plant used in perfume and medicine.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A collocational or collective plant noun, including the cyperus-like rhizome distinguished from related plants by some authorities.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A particular kind of dates.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized plural or collective noun.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A kind of mail coat or garment fabric associated with a place called السَّعْدُ or with Saʿīd ibn al-ʿĀṣ.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used attributively in expressions for particular garments.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A pasture plant, one of the best fodders for camels, whose fresh growth sweetens their milk.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A prickly herb or leguminous plant of the plains; the proverb مَرْعًى وَلَا كَالسَّعْدَانِ praises exceptional excellence.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The prickles of a palm tree.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized nominal use distinct from the pasture plant.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Obedience to God or aid rendered to His cause.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A fixed accusative expression used with سُبْحَانَهُ, as in سُبْحَانَهُ وَسُعْدَانَهُ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The nipple, the areola around it, or the part surrounding the nipple.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An anatomical term motivated by resemblance to the prickly head of the سعدان plant.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The knot of a sandal's thong beneath the sole, next to the ground.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Also called رُغْبَانَةٌ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The knot beneath the pan of a balance.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The plural سَعْدَانَاتٌ denotes the corresponding knots of the scale.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Nail-like structures in the lower parts of certain tendons or sinews.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used in the plural for the structures in the ʿujāyah region.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The callous rounded protuberance on a camel's breast, on which it rests when lying down.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The name is explained by the protuberance's rounded form.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The anus, or its sphincter.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized anatomical use.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The part of a mare's vulva into which the penis enters.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized anatomical use.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A pigeon, or the name of a particular pigeon.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized zoological noun.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A river, rivulet, or irrigation channel that waters the land adjoining it.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: It may denote a small watercourse or a channel carrying irrigation water to cultivated land.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Prosperity, good fortune, happiness, or felicity.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An abstract noun covering religious and worldly felicity; worldly felicity may be psychological, bodily, or due to external circumstances, while the greatest felicity is otherworldly.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Prosperousness, auspiciousness, or luckiness.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used especially of a day, star, or asterism, in opposition to نُحُوسَةٌ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The name of a temple to which members of the Rabīʿah tribe made pilgrimage in pre-Islamic times.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A proper name associated with a sanctuary at Mount Uḥud.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A kind of Yemeni garment or dress.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of garments of the burūd type and of a particular ḥullah; the name is explained either geographically or by association with Saʿīd ibn al-ʿĀṣ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The forearm, or in some usage the upper arm, of a person or animal.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The part between the wrist and elbow, or between the elbow and shoulder according to dialect; the plural is سَوَاعِدُ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An armlet worn on the forearm, made of iron, brass, or gold.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A derived object noun from the bodily sense.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The two wings of a bird.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative anatomical extension of the arm term.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The anterior or primary feathers of a bird's wing.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used in descriptions of a bird's strength or wing structure.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A chief or leading person upon whom others rely.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative use based on the arm's assisting function.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Channels through which water runs to a river, sea, or other watercourse.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: May also denote the channels or outlets from which the water of a well or its springs issues.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The medullary cavities or ducts through which marrow runs in a bone.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative anatomical plural use.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A duct conveying milk to the teat or breast, or the opening from which milk issues.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of the ducts in an animal's udder and, by extension, in a woman's breast.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An affair having several modes of execution and several ways out of it.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Fixed figurative expression describing an undertaking with multiple courses or exits.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The bone of the shank.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized anatomical noun.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A piece of wood set up to support a pulley.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A technical object noun.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A name for the lion.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A proper or epithet-like animal name with irregular declension.

other_classical_meanings.definition: More or most prosperous, fortunate, or happy.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A comparative or superlative epithet applied to a man; its feminine counterpart is reported as سُعْدَى.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A cracking or scab-like skin disease of a camel that makes it weak and decrepit.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized veterinary term, unrelated to the comparative use except in form.

cautions: The displayed Quranic verb follows the QAC passive identification سُعِدَ; the Lane entry also records سَعِدُوا as an alternate reading at the same Quran passage.
Lane's Quran references within the star-name and liturgical discussions are treated as attestations or examples of those Classical expressions, not as additional modern Quran word locations.
